'''Yuri Dmitrievich Burago''' ({{langx|ru|Ю́рий Дми́триевич Бура́го}}; born 21 June 1936)<ref>{{Cite web |title= Персоналии: Бураго Юрий Дмитриевич |trans-title= Personalities: Burago Yuriy Dmitrievich| language= ru |url=https://www.mathnet.ru/php/person.phtml?personid=11320&option_lang=rus |website= mathnet.ru| date= | publisher= |access-date=2024-08-29}}</ref> is a Russian [[mathematician]].  He works in [[differential geometry|differential]] and [[convex geometry]].

== Early life, family and education==
{{expand-section|date= July 2026}}
Burago studied at [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad University]], where he obtained his [[Ph.D.]] and [[Habilitation]] degrees. His advisors were [[Victor Zalgaller]] and [[Aleksandr Danilovich Aleksandrov|Aleksandr Aleksandrov]].

==Career==
Yuri Burago created what is known now as Alexandrov Geometry with his students [[Grigori Perelman]] and Petrunin, and [[Mikhael Gromov (mathematician)|M. Gromov]]. Also brought geometric inequalities to the state of art.

Burago is the head of the Laboratory of Geometry and Topology that is part of the [[St. Petersburg Department of Steklov Institute of Mathematics of Russian Academy of Sciences|St. Petersburg Department of Steklov Institute of Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.pdmi.ras.ru/eng/labs/topologie.php |title= Laboratory of Geometry and Topology |website= pdmi.ras.ru| publisher= St. Petersburg Department of V. A. Steklov Institute of Mathematics of the Russian Academy of Sciences |access-date= 2026-07-05}}</ref> He took part in a report for the United States Civilian Research and Development Foundation for the Independent States of the former [[Soviet Union]].<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.crdf.org/usr_doc/2001ProgramReport.pdf |title= 2001 Program Report |website= crdf.org |publisher= US Civilian Research and Development Foundation for the Independent States of the former Soviet Union |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20061207035527/http://www.crdf.org/usr_doc/2001ProgramReport.pdf |archive-date= 2006-12-07 |url-status= dead |access-date= }}</ref>

==Students==
He has advised [[Grigori Perelman]], who solved the [[Poincaré conjecture]], one of the seven [[Clay Mathematics Institute|Millennium Prize Problems]]. Burago was an advisor to Perelman during the latter's [[post-graduate]] research at [[St. Petersburg Department of Steklov Institute of Mathematics of Russian Academy of Sciences|St. Petersburg Department of Steklov Institute of Mathematics]].
